project.name: portal-libs
project.description:
The words the PORTAL's repositories share with each other and with nobody else.
The estate has a shared kernel (../../shared) and it is not this. The kernel is what the two PRODUCTS share — identity, and the generic mechanisms any service would want: a unit of work, an outbox, an envelope, a clock. What lives HERE speaks the portal's own domain: a meme, its thread, an author, what may be kept of a leaver's content. The F1 game has no use for a single one of these words, and putting them in the kernel meant the kernel knew what a meme was.
That is not a hypothetical tidiness argument. These three libraries sat in `shared/` until 2026-09-28 and none of them was ever listed among the kernel's libraries in `shared/CLAUDE.md` — they arrived one at a time, each an obvious place for one more cross-repository word, because there WAS no other place. Four portal repositories need a vocabulary none of them can own; the only home the estate offered was the kernel. This repository is that missing home.
The dependency direction is the whole point and it runs one way: these modules depend on the kernel (`unit-of-work`, `user-id`), and nothing in the kernel depends on them. `account-closure` deliberately stayed behind — microservice-security reads its ClosureMessages, so it is the contract BETWEEN identity and the portal, and identity is shared with the game.
A pure aggregator, NOT the parent of the modules: every one stays buildable on its own, the estate's rule everywhere.
